headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Roo Code can overwrite files and run shell commands while Haystack can call MCP/REST and broad egress, creating dangerous default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, and Roo Code can read/write VS Code workspace files and run browsers. If Haystack ingests Roo-generated content from a shared workspace or MCP channel, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Haystack reads Roo-authored workspace files as instructions or prompts, injection risk is active.
IF both agents share an MCP server without provenance tagging, injected content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable MCP on the shared path.
Require explicit prompt delimiters for any file-fed content.
Add provenance labels before passing outputs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints. In a shared workspace, Roo can expose code or screenshots that Haystack may transmit outward. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory, code and screenshots can flow from Roo to Haystack.
IF Haystack forwards retrieved file contents to external APIs, those contents can leave the environment.
mitigations: Use separate repositories or workspace roots.
Turn off automatic file ingestion in Haystack.
Redact screenshots and secrets before handoff.
Restrict Haystack egress to approved endpoints only.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and per-workspace shared state via filesystem; Haystack can also use MCP and broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The conflict is dangerous by default because Roo explicitly supports shared filesystem state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same VS Code workspace, file races are possible.
IF both modify git state without an external lock, commits or branches can diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign one agent per workspace.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Require manual review before any commit.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent and Roo Code can act on code, shell, and browser tasks. If Haystack’s retrieved facts are passed into Roo without verification, Roo may execute or commit incorrect actions. The pair does not document a built-in verification step, so the cascade is plausible but not automatically catastrophic.
conditions: IF Haystack outputs are treated as authoritative by Roo Code, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Roo uses retrieved text to generate commits or shell commands without review, errors cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before actions.
Require Roo to cite source snippets before acting.
Use a second-pass verifier on Haystack outputs.
Limit Roo to read-only mode for retrieval tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys. The pair can therefore mix telemetry with code and secrets, creating retention and residency questions. No profile shows a compliance boundary or DPA, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF screenshots or source code are logged alongside telemetry, retention policy mismatch exists.
IF model-provider keys are stored or forwarded outside the intended region, residency/compliance issues arise.
mitigations: Disable nonessential telemetry.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Avoid placing secrets in shared workspaces.
Confirm data-processing terms before production use.
